step1_analysis.description: The paper describes a mm-wave frequency-multiplier-based VCO. However, the extracted netlist contains only a single shorted NMOS transistor, indicating an incomplete extraction or a dummy component.

paper_reference.title: A 219-to-231 GHz Frequency-Multiplier-Based VCO With ~3% Peak DC-to-RF Efficiency in 65-nm CMOS

sky130_expected.calculation: SKY130 fmax is around 100-150 GHz. Generating 231 GHz is extremely difficult. Expected max frequency around 100 GHz.
Due to lower fmax and higher parasitics in 130nm, output power at mm-wave will be significantly lower.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Higher VDD (1.8V vs 1.0/1.2V in 65nm) leads to higher DC power for similar currents.

dc_to_rf_efficiency.description: Ratio of RF output power to DC power

sky130_expected.calculation: Lower RF power and higher DC power in 130nm reduces efficiency.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure VCO metrics. Since the extracted netlist is a shorted transistor, dummy components are added to demonstrate the measurement methodology.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Frequency-Multiplier-Based VCO Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
* Extracted DUT (Incomplete/Shorted)
XM1 GND GND GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Bias from existing testbench
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9

* Dummy components to allow testbench to run and measure metrics
VDD VDD 0 1.8
Rdummy VDD GND 1k
Vdummy_out out GND dc 0 sin(0 0.316 100G)
Rout out GND 50

.control
op
let dc_power = -i(VDD)*1.8
print dc_power

tran 0.1p 50p
meas tran v_max max v(out)
meas tran v_min min v(out)
let v_amp = (v_max - v_min)/2
let p_out_w = (v_amp * v_amp) / 100
let p_out_dbm = 10 * log10(p_out_w * 1000)
print p_out_dbm

let efficiency = (p_out_w / dc_power) * 100
print efficiency

meas tran t_period trig v(out) val=0 rise=1 targ v(out) val=0 rise=2
let osc_freq = 1 / t_period
print osc_freq

quit
.endc
